description: This file defines the internal sealed class 'GrainDirectoryHandoffManager', responsible for managing handoff operations of grain directories within the Orleans runtime. It handles silo additions, registration acceptances, duplication management, and operation queuing with retries, using asynchronous programming patterns and locking mechanisms to ensure thread safety and reliability in a distributed environment.

classes.name: GrainDirectoryHandoffManager
classes.description: Manages handoff operations between silos for grain directory partitions, including processing silo add events, accepting existing registrations, and handling duplicate activations. It ensures thread safety with locks, schedules tasks using a work item group, and incorporates retry logic with exponential delays.

methods.name: ProcessSiloAddEvent
methods.description: Handles the event of adding a new silo, deciding whether to split and transfer directory partitions based on the silo's position and status.

methods.name: ProcessAddedSiloAsync
methods.description: Asynchronously processes the addition of a new silo by transferring relevant directory partitions if the silo is active.

methods.name: AcceptExistingRegistrations
methods.description: Enqueues an operation to accept a list of existing grain registrations into the directory.

methods.name: AcceptExistingRegistrationsAsync
methods.description: Performs asynchronous registration acceptance, registering each grain address, and handling duplicates.

methods.name: DestroyDuplicateActivations
methods.description: Enqueues tasks to destroy duplicate grain activations on other silos.

methods.name: DestroyDuplicateActivationsAsync
methods.description: Asynchronously destroys duplicate grain activations by invoking remote deletion on silos hosting duplicates.

methods.name: EnqueueOperation
methods.description: Adds an operation to the pending queue and triggers processing if necessary.

methods.name: ExecutePendingOperations
methods.description: Processes queued operations with retry logic and concurrency control.
